> "To address these uses, this memo reserves a path prefix in HTTP, HTTPS, WebSocket (WS), and Secure WebSocket (WSS) URIs for these "well-known locations", "/.well-known/"."

Section 3 gives the definition: "A well-known URI is a URI [RFC3986] whose path component begins with the characters "/.well-known/", provided that the scheme is explicitly defined to support well-known URIs." It's rooted at the top of the path only — "/foo/.well-known/example" is not a well-known URI.

**Registration policy: Specification Required, on the advice of one or more experts**

> "Well-known URIs are registered on the advice of one or more experts, with a Specification Required (using terminology from [RFC8126])."

Section 3 adds the applicant-side rule: "Applications that wish to mint new well-known URIs MUST register them, following the procedures in Section 5.1, subject to the following requirements." Registrations carry a status of "permanent" or "provisional"; Standards Track and other open-standard values are permanent, others provisional unless the experts find them in use.

**URI schemes: http, https, ws, wss**

> "This specification updates the "http" [RFC7230] and "https" [RFC7230] schemes to support well-known URIs."

The WebSocket pair comes in through a separate document, as the same paragraph says: "Other existing schemes can use the appropriate process for updating their definitions; for example, [RFC8307] does so for the "ws" and "wss" schemes." The document's Table 1 lists those four against RFC 8615 and RFC 8307, plus coap, coap+tcp, coap+ws, coaps, coaps+tcp and coaps+ws via RFC 7252 and RFC 8323.

Other schemes are not covered by default: "Well-known URIs can also be used with other URI schemes, but only when those schemes' definitions explicitly allow it." And for registrations that name no scheme: "If no URI schemes are explicitly specified, "http" and "https" are assumed."
